Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11

Class X11ShmExt

java.lang.Object
gnu.x11.extension.Extension
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11.X11ShmExt
public class X11ShmExt extends gnu.x11.extension.Extension
Pure-Java Escher binding for the MIT Shared Memory extension (MIT-SHM).

MIT-SHM allows a client to share a memory segment with the X server so that pixel data can be transferred without copying over the socket. For a compositor reading back redirected window contents at interactive frame rates, this is the difference between ~5 ms (shm) and ~50 ms (socket round-trip) per full-screen readback.

Protocol reference: MIT-SHM Extension, Version 1.1.

Shared memory segment lifecycle

The X protocol's ShmAttach request takes a SysV shared memory id (the integer returned by shmget(2)). Obtaining that id requires a POSIX syscall that pure Java on JDK 21 cannot make without the Foreign Function & Memory API (preview in 21, final in 22). This class therefore provides the protocol bindings only; the caller must supply a valid shmid obtained by one of:

  • A tiny native helper invoked via ProcessBuilder (e.g. a compiled C one-liner or python3 -c "import ctypes; ...").
  • JDK 22+ java.lang.foreign.Linker (no preview flag needed).
  • The lg3d LFS build can ship a /usr/lib/lg3d/shm-helper binary that prints the shmid to stdout.

If no shm segment is available, Stage 3's CompositeWindowImageLoader falls back to the core Drawable.image(int, int, int, int, int, int) (XGetImage) request, which is slower but requires no shared memory.

  • Method Details

    • attach

      public void attach(int shmseg, int shmid, boolean read_only)
      Attaches a SysV shared memory segment to the X connection. After this call, the server maps the segment identified by shmid into its address space and the client can use shmseg in PutImage, GetImage, and CreatePixmap requests.
      Parameters:
      shmseg - a pre-allocated X resource id for the segment (display.allocate_id())
      shmid - the SysV shared memory id from shmget(2)
      read_only - true if the server will only read from the segment

    • detach

      public void detach(int shmseg)
      Detaches a previously attached shared memory segment. The server unmaps its copy; the client should then shmdt(2) and shmctl(IPC_RMID) on its side.

    • putImage

      public void putImage(gnu.x11.Drawable drawable, gnu.x11.GC gc, int shmseg, int total_width, int total_height, int src_x, int src_y, int src_width, int src_height, int dst_x, int dst_y, int depth, int format, boolean send_event, int offset)
      Copies pixel data from the shared memory segment into a drawable. This is the fast path for uploading lg3d-rendered content back to an X window (e.g. for the overlay or for unredirected windows).
      Parameters:
      drawable - destination
      gc - graphics context
      shmseg - attached shared memory segment
      total_width - width of the image in the shm segment
      total_height - height of the image in the shm segment
      src_x - source rectangle x within the shm image
      src_y - source rectangle y
      src_width - source rectangle width
      src_height - source rectangle height
      dst_x - destination x on the drawable
      dst_y - destination y on the drawable
      depth - depth of the image
      format - FORMAT_ZPIXMAP or FORMAT_PIXMAP
      send_event - if true, the server sends a ShmCompletion event
      offset - byte offset within the shm segment

    • getImage

      public X11ShmExt.GetImageReply getImage(gnu.x11.Drawable drawable, int shmseg, int x, int y, int width, int height, int plane_mask, int format, int offset)
      Reads pixel data from a drawable into the shared memory segment. This is the fast path for the compositor: instead of sending pixels over the socket (core GetImage), the server writes directly into the shm segment that the client has already mapped.
      Parameters:
      drawable - source drawable (typically a NameWindowPixmap)
      shmseg - attached shared memory segment
      x - source x
      y - source y
      width - source width
      height - source height
      plane_mask - plane mask (AllPlanes = -1)
      format - FORMAT_ZPIXMAP
      offset - byte offset within the shm segment to write into
      Returns:
      reply containing depth, visual, and size metadata

    • createPixmap

      public void createPixmap(gnu.x11.Pixmap pixmap, gnu.x11.Drawable drawable, int width, int height, int depth, int shmseg, int offset)
      Creates a pixmap backed by the shared memory segment. Drawing into this pixmap writes directly to the shm memory, which the client can then read without any X protocol round-trip. Requires SHM 1.1+ and shared_pixmaps_supported.
      Parameters:
      pixmap - pre-allocated pixmap id
      drawable - a drawable of the same depth (used for the screen)
      width - pixmap width
      height - pixmap height
      depth - pixmap depth
      shmseg - attached shared memory segment
      offset - byte offset within the segment

    • freePixmap

      public void freePixmap(gnu.x11.Pixmap pixmap)
      Frees a pixmap created with createPixmap(gnu.x11.Pixmap, gnu.x11.Drawable, int, int, int, int, int). The underlying shm segment is not detached; call detach(int) separately.
